items.name: app-settings-core
items.title: App Settings core
items.description: The transport, hooks and provider every App Settings component reads. Install this alone to build your own UI over App Settings resolutions with React Query.
items.author: Connor Doman <connor@connordoman.dev>
items.docs: Wrap your settings page in <AppSettingsProvider transport={...}>. Use transportFromClient(new AppSettingsClient({ ... })) to talk to App Settings directly, or createHttpTransport({ resolve, write }) to go through your own API. Set SETTINGS_URL and SETTINGS_API_KEY server-side; never ship an API key to the browser.

items.name: setting-inputs
items.title: Setting inputs
items.description: One control per setting type — BOOLEAN, NUMBER, STRING, DATETIME, SELECT and JSON — plus the dispatcher that picks between them and the context that lets you swap any of them out.
items.author: Connor Doman <connor@connordoman.dev>

items.name: setting-field
items.title: Setting field
items.description: A labelled setting row: name, description, the right control for its type, the layer its value came from, and the badge that says a group policy is holding it in place.
items.author: Connor Doman <connor@connordoman.dev>

items.name: setting-list
items.title: Setting list
items.description: A whole resolution as sections of setting rows, each writing as it changes. The switchboard.
items.author: Connor Doman <connor@connordoman.dev>

items.name: settings-form
items.title: Settings form
items.description: Many settings edited together and saved in one go, with a sticky footer that counts what is pending and keeps the rows that failed.
items.author: Connor Doman <connor@connordoman.dev>

items.name: app-settings
items.title: App Settings UI
items.description: Everything: the core hooks, every input, the field, the list and the form. Start here for an admin switchboard.
items.author: Connor Doman <connor@connordoman.dev>
